_march.2026-07-28-routed-rebaseline: RE-BASELINED against the routed board on the owner's explicit instruction. 556ccf4f committed the first route (51 of 96 nets), so the board now carries 2338 track segments and 48 vias; the previous ceilings (85 errors / 578 warnings) were measured on an UNROUTED board, so the gate was comparing two different artifacts. nondeterministic_error_types.note: These three vary run-to-run on a byte-identical board (sha256 below constant throughout; measured 11 times). Their ceilings are deliberately set ABOVE the observed maximum, with headroom, because a ceiling at the observed max still failed 1 run in 3. They are guard-rails against a catastrophic regression, not ratchet targets, and they must NOT be read as the board's measured state. Ratcheting them is meaningless until the non-determinism is fixed -- most likely zone filling, since the gate's run_drc fills zones first and a raw `kicad-cli pcb drc` yields different numbers. Leaving them tight would produce an intermittently-red gate, which gets masked as flake; that is exactly how the benders_loop capability removal stayed hidden behind a 'JAX nondeterministic' comment for months. The other 8 error types and all 10 warning types were identical on every run and ARE ratchetable.
